transitions.historical_text: You can only use this card's effect once, and only during this turn. When a monster on your side of the field is sent to your Graveyard, you can Special Summon 1 monster with an ATK of 1500 points or less from your Deck. Then shuffle your Deck.
transitions.modern_text: If a monster on your side of the field was sent to your Graveyard this turn, you can Special Summon 1 monster with an ATK of 1500 points or less from your Deck once during this turn. Then shuffle your Deck.
transitions.summary: The TP7 text revision changed the condition from a forward-looking send after Last Will resolves to a turn-wide condition that can already be satisfied by an earlier send in the same turn. The pinned GOAT script installs an EVENT_TO_GRAVE watcher at resolution; the modern script uses a global turn flag.

coverage.gap_reason: Project Ignis ships no implementation matching this version: none of the upstream historical variants in the pinned databases carries this version's card text. Reproducing it needs a custom script and a reserved passcode.

gap.behavioural_impact: Period ruling package on top of the text change. The usage-window and chain-procedure transitions are separately bounded by period ruling attestations, while activation legality remains undated. Activation condition: the modern `s.spcon`/`s.activate` both require `Duel.IsExistingMatchingCard(s.spfilter,tp,LOCATION_DECK,...)` before offering the Summon, while the goat `s.checkop2` prompts and consumes the effect regardless of whether a monster with 1500 or less ATK is in the Deck. Failed-search verification: the goat operation calls `Duel.GoatConfirm(tp,LOCATION_DECK)` when the selection comes back empty.

review.notes: The official Konami card database lists TP7-EN015 with the revised "was sent ... this turn" text and the project release ledger records Tournament Pack 7 on 2005-11-01. That printing directly establishes the retroactivity transition only. Pre-TP7 Ian Estrin material positively attests the first-opportunity usage rule around 2005-01-20, while Curtis Schultz's June 2006 post-errata material attests later use; usage-window is therefore a separate bounded ruling event, not an exact TP7 transition. Period judge material likewise treats the old state as using the Chain, while the post-errata explanation says the Summon does not use the Chain; chain-procedure is a separate bounded ruling event. Activation legality with no eligible Deck target and failed-search Deck verification remain distinct ruling questions with no sourced co-occurrence. The verification event retains the shared TCG procedure bounds: old behavior is positively attested through 2011-02-02 and the first located modern no-verification policy is 2019-04-03. The three ruling events are independent of TP7 except that each is represented with its strongest available bounds; the date-proven ordering graph has only c0 -> c4, c1 -> c4, and c2 -> c4. The intermediate TP7 text with the old ruling package has no upstream implementation and remains a known gap at {c0}.
